module purpose: neorv32_onewire is a memory-mapped single-wire serial controller: bus writes configure enable and timing settings and enqueue command/data words, while internal timing and serial logic drive onewire_o and sample onewire_i. It returns status and captured results through bus_rsp_o, exports clkgen_en_o, and raises irq_o when enabled and idle with no pending transmit data.

use-case flows.value: control settings written into the internal control register: enable, clear pulse, clock prescaler, and clock divider
a command-plus-byte word written into the transmit path and taken up by the serial engine when data is available
a programmable serial tick generated from clkgen_i using the stored prescaler and divider
serial execution that drives the output line, samples the input line, shifts sampled bits, detects presence, and finishes a command
interrupt request asserted when enabled and the controller is idle with no pending transmit data
control and status values returned on a control-register read: enable, clock settings, FIFO status, line sense, and busy state
captured receive result returned on a data-register read: byte value and presence bit
control, timing, interrupt, serial state, and output forced to known values by rstn_i='0', with transmit and receive FIFOs cleared when disabled or when clear is requested

conceptual assets.reasoning: A bus write stores the enable bit at line 142. The stored value is read back at line 150, exported on clkgen_en_o at line 273, forces FIFO clearing when low at lines 199 and 231, holds the clock counter reset at line 258, participates in irq generation at line 243, and is copied into the serial state at line 311. These configure, operate, report, and reset flows depend on the integrity of this held setting; availability is also established because operation can proceed only when it is set.

conceptual assets.concept: Software clear request pulse for the transmit and receive queues
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control logic forces ctrl.clear low each cycle at line 140 and writes a new pulse from the control register at line 143. That stored event is consumed by the FIFO-clear conditions at lines 199 and 231. Integrity matters because an unintended clear drops queued transmit commands or captured receive results, while a missed clear leaves stale queue contents; availability of the clear action is established because the pulse is used immediately in both clear conditions.

The prescaler and divider fields are stored at lines 144-145 and read back at lines 151-152. The clock generator uses them at lines 260-263 to decide when clk_tick is asserted from the selected clk_src input, and that tick then gates transmit dequeue and serial progress at lines 202, 329, 346, 360, and 366. Corrupt timing settings therefore make the implemented transfer schedule incorrect; availability is established when the controller is enabled and the selected clock source bit becomes active.

conceptual assets.concept: Queued operation command and associated byte value to be executed by the serial engine
conceptual assets.reasoning: A write to the data register forms the transmit word at line 201 and presents it to the TX FIFO at line 190. When data is available, the serial engine leaves idle at lines 317-318; the dequeued word from fifo.tx_rdata selects the command case at lines 323 and 331-335 and loads the working byte into serial.sreg at line 328. Integrity matters because these fields determine which operation runs and what byte is shifted; availability is established because available TX entries are taken into execution. The FIFO's internal storage is inside an instantiated sub-unit, so the visible realization points are its local write-side and read-side signals and the loaded working register.

conceptual assets.concept: Operation progress state and its busy/not-busy decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: Progress is held in serial.state, serial.bit_cnt, and serial.tick_cnt. The case on serial.state at line 312 selects idle, load, slot, and reset behavior; line 318 starts a command when TX data is available; lines 350-361 and 366-380 advance or terminate slot/reset timing; and line 354 detects the last bit. serial.busy is computed at line 394 from serial.state(1 downto 0) and is then used for status readout at line 159, interrupt generation at line 243, and output-drive behavior at line 299. Integrity matters because command execution, completion, and idle reporting depend on these state values and this decision; availability is established because, with TX data and ticks, the sequence reaches completion at lines 355 or 379.

The serial engine decides when to drive or release the output line: serial.wire_lo is asserted at lines 330 and 358, serial.wire_hi is asserted at lines 343 and 371, and onewire_o is updated by lines 299-302. Integrity matters because external logic sees exactly these driven values during operation; availability is established because active commands generate output transitions under the stored timing and progress conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: Captured input result byte and presence indication
conceptual assets.reasoning: Incoming line values are sampled from onewire_i into serial.wire_in at line 296. A read-slot sample is taken at line 347 and shifted into serial.sreg at line 352, while a separate indication is captured at line 375 and stored in serial.presence. The result word serial.presence & serial.sreg is then presented to the RX FIFO at line 232 and written on completion at line 233; lines 161-162 later return that stored result. Integrity matters because the receiving consumer must get exactly the captured byte and indication; availability is established when completion causes the write.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt request for the enabled idle-with-empty-transmit condition
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_o is updated at line 243 with the predicate `ctrl.enable and (not fifo.tx_avail) and (not serial.busy)` and reset at line 241. This is the module's report flow for its enabled-and-idle condition with no pending transmit data. Integrity matters because external logic depends on the exact predicate; availability is also established because the registered output is produced on each rising edge while that predicate holds.
